description: A composite figure of six panels in two rows that mixes three kinds of image — 3-D fracture-surface height maps, whole-fracture SEM images and high-magnification SEM images; row (a) is the LN steel, row (b) the HN steel. Left column: colour-coded 3-D surface reconstructions plotted over in-plane axes of 0–10.00 mm x 0–10.00 mm with rainbow colour bars; (a) spans 0.00–12.19 mm and shows a tall red/pink dome, (b) spans 0.00–8.09 mm and shows a lower, flatter green/blue plateau. Middle column: low-magnification SEM fractographs of the whole circular fracture surface, each with a 1 mm scale bar and a small white square marking the region shown at right; (a) is a relatively flat, rough section, (b) shows a crater (cup-and-cone) outline with concentric rings. Right column: SEM of the boxed areas at 5 µm scale bars — (a) dense, small equiaxed dimples; (b) larger, deeper, more uniformly distributed dimples. The group argues that HN steel fails with a coarser, deeper-dimpled crater-shaped fracture consistent with better plasticity and toughness, while LN shows finer, more numerous dimples and a flatter section; no dimple dimensions are printed.

subfigures.description: 3-D colour-coded height map of the LN tensile fracture surface; colour bar 0.00–12.19 mm, in-plane axes 0–10.00 mm, showing a high red/pink dome-shaped peak on a blue base.

Low-magnification SEM image of the entire LN fracture surface, 1 mm scale bar; surface is rough and relatively flat with dark porosity-like features, and a white square marks the region magnified at right.
High-magnification SEM (5 µm scale bar) of the boxed LN region: numerous small, shallow equiaxed dimples.
3-D colour-coded height map of the HN tensile fracture surface; colour bar 0.00–8.09 mm, in-plane axes 0–10.00 mm, showing a lower, flatter green/blue plateau.
Low-magnification SEM image of the entire HN fracture surface, 1 mm scale bar; crater/cup-and-cone outline with concentric rings, and a small white square marking the region magnified at right.
High-magnification SEM (5 µm scale bar) of the boxed HN region: larger, deeper dimples more uniformly distributed, with some fine dimples between them.

observations.observation: The left panel of row (a) is a 3-D surface height map whose colour bar is scaled 0.00 to 12.19 mm, with both in-plane axes labelled 0 to 10.00 mm.
The left panel of row (b) is a 3-D surface height map whose colour bar is scaled 0.00 to 8.09 mm, with both in-plane axes labelled 0 to 10.00 mm.
The 3-D maps show a much taller red/pink dome for (a) than the flatter green/blue plateau of (b); the printed maximum heights are 12.19 mm for (a) and 8.09 mm for (b).

The middle panels are SEM images of the complete circular tensile fracture surface, each annotated with a 1 mm scale bar and a white square indicating the area magnified in the corresponding right-hand panel.
The middle image of (b) shows a crater (cup-and-cone) fracture outline with concentric ring markings, whereas the middle image of (a) shows a rougher, flatter fracture section.
The right-hand panels are high-magnification SEM images with 5 µm scale bars; (a) shows many small dimples while (b) shows larger, deeper and more uniformly distributed dimples.
The caption identifies (a) as the LN steel and (b) as the HN steel tensile fracture morphologies.

The caption states that the macroscopic necking degree of the HN steel was considerably greater than that of the LN steel, although the 3-D height maps in the figure show a taller reconstructed surface for LN (12.19 mm) than for HN (8.09 mm); the panels do not label what the mapped height represents.
The citing text reports that large dimples were observed in the HN steel fractures, usually surrounded by small dimples.
The citing text reports that dimples in the LN steel were smaller in size and greater in number, indicating more severe local stress concentration of the LN steel during deformation.

The citing text states the fracture morphology of the HN steel had a crater shape, whereas the LN steel fracture section was 45° to the load direction, implying shear-stress fracture before reaching tensile strength.

The citing text attributes the improved plasticity and fracture toughness of the HN steel to fine grains and many twins relieving stress concentration, with grain and twin boundaries preventing crack propagation.

unreadable_items: the physical meaning/quantity of the 3-D map height axis is not labelled (only the numeric range in mm is printed)
no numerical dimple sizes or distributions are printed on the 5 µm SEM panels (only visible by eye)
